v4.9.067 - a restore point can no longer cost you the project

#328 The terminal makes one sound when it needs an answer and another when it
     has finished, so you can tell them apart without looking.
#329 Every push wrote the whole project - drawings and all - into a single
     database value as a restore point. Past the size limit for one value that
     threw, and the push threw with it, so nothing at all was written: not the
     snapshot, not the frames, not the work. Every retry did the same and the
     project became permanently unsyncable, with a bare 500 as the only sign.
     An oversized project now goes without a restore point and says so, and the
     whole call is wrapped besides. A restore point is a courtesy; the work is
     not.
#330 A new index on images.r2_key. Looking up an image was reading every image
     row belonging to every user, on every single fetch - so opening a
     forty-frame storyboard did forty full scans, and it got slower every day.
